## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

Linguistically, the verses of the text display notable clustering of verbal forms, such as repeated tokens of the thematic aorist *(ni)patāmase* [Kingsbury 2002].
Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral list four translations across four languages [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus reports extensive Pali text reuse with its commentary in the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* (Catuttho bhāgo; 206 matches across 54,489 characters) and a short segment shared with the *Daddallavimānavatthu* (Vv 34) [DharmaNexus]. In cross-language automated alignments, DharmaNexus detects textual affinities with the Chinese *Madhyama Āgama* (T 26), the Tibetan *Śārdūlakarṇāvadāna* (D 358), the Sanskrit *Āryamañjuśrīmūlakalpa*, and the Chinese *Saṃyuktāgama* (T 99) [DharmaNexus].
